description: This exists because the audit that produced it was a one-off: a person wondered how far behind the stack was, checked seventeen images by hand, and found swagger-ui two years old and PostgREST two majors back. Nothing would have raised either again. The point of this file is that the CHECK happens on a schedule. Deciding what to merge stays a human job, and several rules below exist to keep it that way.

WHAT A NAIVE CONFIGURATION WOULD GET WRONG HERE, and why packageRules is the long half: the Supabase components are a COORDINATED SET that upstream tests together. Measured against Docker Hub, gotrue v2.189.0 and postgres-meta v0.96.6 look outdated. They are in fact the exact versions upstream pins, and bumping them would move this stack OFF the tested combination. Renovate cannot read upstream's compose file, so it must not be trusted to propose those individually.

THE DASHBOARD IS THE DELIVERABLE, more than the PRs are. It is one issue listing every available update including the ones deliberately held back, which is exactly the artefact the manual audit produced and then threw away.

SCHEDULING IS MONTHLY, AND THE WORKFLOW CRON IS NOT. Routine currency work opens on the first of the month (the window is the whole day, since the cron that invokes Renovate fires hours after its nominal time and a morning window never matched), because a weekly batch of pull requests is a standing tax on whoever has to read them and the thing being defended against moves over months, not days. The workflow that INVOKES Renovate still runs daily, and that is deliberate rather than sloppy: Renovate can only act while the process is running, so a monthly cron would silently make vulnerabilityAlerts monthly too -- and those are supposed to ignore the schedule entirely. Daily invocation plus a monthly window means routine noise once a month and a security advisory picked up within a day. A release must be three days old before it becomes a PR, so one that is pulled within days never does; vulnerability alerts are exempt from that wait.

packageRules.description: Images built from this repository. The tag is set at deploy time and is empty in values.yaml, so there is no upstream to track.

THE COORDINATED SET. One PR or none: these move together upstream and are tested together, and the correct target is usually upstream Supabase's own pin rather than the newest tag. dependencyDashboardApproval means Renovate lists them and waits to be asked, because the decision needs a person to compare against supabase/supabase docker/docker-compose.yml. See issue #49.

THE DENO THAT RESOLVES THE EDGE FUNCTIONS is the Deno supabase/edge-runtime embeds (`edge-runtime --version`), not the newest: the functions image's `modules` stage and the top-level constraints.deno (which the deno manager maintains supabase/functions/deno.lock with) both name it, and a lock written by another Deno can be a format the build cannot read. It moves by hand when edge-runtime does.
The historian. Not grouped with anything: a patch bump is usually safe and is still the one change that can take the telemetry store with it.

A major version is a reading task before it is a merge task. Held on the dashboard so it is proposed deliberately -- Kong 3.0, for one, silently switched off every per-service Prometheus metric while leaving the scrape target green.
Security updates outrank everything else in the queue.
Workflow actions: one PR, since they are independent of everything the stack runs.
